variants.name: Spring @Transactional service method
variants.implementation_notes: Mainstream Java: the script is a public method on a @Service bean and the transaction boundary is metadata - @Transactional (or jakarta.transaction.Transactional) makes the container start a transaction before the method and commit it on normal return, rolling back on RuntimeException. The method body stays a straight line of repository/gateway calls. Explicit begin/commit is only justified when the script spans several resources, needs a specific isolation level or savepoint, or must make a checked exception roll back (rollbackFor); remember that the annotation only takes effect through the Spring proxy, so self-invocation and private methods run without it.
pitfalls: Self-invocation (this.otherScript()) bypasses the proxy, so the inner call runs with no transaction and no rollback rules.
Default rollback covers unchecked exceptions only: a checked exception committed by accident is a data-integrity bug, so set rollbackFor where calls are mixed.
The whole method runs inside one transaction: HTTP calls, message sends and slow work inside it hold row locks for their duration.

variants.name: JDBC service method with manual transaction control
variants.implementation_notes: The container-free realization: the script disables auto-commit on a JDBC connection, runs its prepared statements, calls commit() once and rolls back in the catch path (savepoints give partial rollback). Prefer it for batch jobs, for code without a DI container, or when the script needs direct control of isolation level and read-only mode; restore auto-commit before returning the connection to a pool and wrap connection handling in try-with-resources.
pitfalls: Returning a connection to the pool without restoring auto-commit poisons the next borrower.
A missing rollback on the checked-exception path leaves the transaction - and its row locks - open.
Isolation defaults differ per driver and per database; state the level explicitly when the script's correctness depends on it.
